answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when an adjudicated claim is fraudulent. A zephyr of newly minted accounts therefore gains no influence for free: each must tie up real capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it. The thread of evidence linking submissions to the same beneficial owner can raise the required stake or trigger review, while an atlas of past outcomes helps set risk-based thresholds. The attacker pays in capital and loses it if caught.
